// Stat caps. Default to the stock conf/battle/player.conf values, so worlds that
// set none of these in their env file are unaffected.
//
// These are the ceiling on what a raised level cap can actually buy: in
// pre-renewal it costs 3768 status points to take all six stats to 99, and the
// stock statpoint table already hands out 4545 by level 200 — so at a cap of 99
// the stats are saturated by base level 181 and every level after that is
// cosmetic. See SETUP.md, "Per-world level cap".
//
// There are NINE caps, applied per class family by pc_maxparameter /
// JobDatabase::loadingFinished (src/map/pc.cpp:14338). Only these three can be
// reached in pre-renewal, and max_parameter alone would leave every
// transcendent job (Lord Knight, High Priest, …) — the actual endgame — at 99.
// The other six (third/fourth/extended/summoner/trait) are renewal-only here.
max_parameter: ${MAX_PARAMETER}
max_trans_parameter: ${MAX_TRANS_PARAMETER}
max_baby_parameter: ${MAX_BABY_PARAMETER}

// Other per-world rates go here, e.g.:
//
//   base_exp_rate: 100
//   job_exp_rate: 100
//   item_rate_common: 100
//
// Hardcoding them applies them to every world, since all worlds render from this
// one template. To vary them per world, add the variable to .env.world-<id>,
// list it in the TOKENS array in render-assets.sh, and reference it here in
// dollar-brace form. A placeholder left unresolved aborts the render, so a token
// added here without a matching env entry fails loudly rather than silently
// emitting an empty value.
//
// NOTE: this comment cannot itself show a dollar-brace example — render-assets.sh
// greps the output for leftover placeholders and would abort on it.
